Class goals 10 min for the warm up

Module 3 · Class 2 · Technology, society and the environment

By the end of this class you can:

  • give advice with should and talk about rules with must, mustn't, have to, can;
  • talk about possibility with might;
  • read a guide, listen to a conversation, create rules with your class and write advice for a classmate.

Warm-up: Sign match 8 min

Two teams · Memory game: match each sign with its rule

Flip two cards: one sign and one sentence. If they match, your team gets a point and plays again. If not, the cards turn over and the other team plays. Remember where the cards are!

Modal verbs 15 min for the whole tab

After a modal verb we use the base form: You should recycle, not You should to recycle.

UseModalExample
Adviceshould / shouldn'tYou should use the online library.
Strong rulemust / have toYou must show your student card.
Prohibitionmustn't / can'tYou mustn't use your phone in the exam.
Not necessarydon't have toYou don't have to buy the book. It's free online.
Permissioncan / can'tYou can borrow a laptop.
PossibilitymightIt might rain. Take an umbrella.

Be careful!

  • mustn't = forbidden. You mustn't eat in the lab.
  • don't have to = it is not necessary. You don't have to book.

Questions

  • Can I use my phone here?
  • Should I save my files?
  • Do I have to book a computer?

Practice

Green Campus Guide 13 min

Reading an informative leaflet

Read the guide. Underline the modal verbs. Then do the activities.

Green Campus Guide

Welcome to our university! Follow these rules and tips to protect the environment and use technology well.

Rules. You must separate your rubbish in the green, yellow and blue bins. You must turn off the lights in empty classrooms. You mustn't leave computers on when you leave the lab.

Tips. You should bring a reusable bottle. You should use the online library instead of printing. You shouldn't print everything: read on your tablet.

Good to know. You can borrow a laptop from the library with your student card. You don't have to buy paper books: many are available online. You might find free courses on the university platform.

Reading activities

At the help desk 12 min

Listening to a conversation

Before you listen

It is Sofía's first day at university. She asks about the computer lab. Talk to a partner: what rules do you think there are?

Audio

Press Play. Listen two times. Do the activities below.

After you listen: your turn

Think about a place at your university (the library, the lab, the cafeteria). Tell your partner two rules or tips for new students, then write them.

Class Parliament 15 min

Speaking · Create and vote on rules for your class

Work in groups. Your group proposes five rules for using technology and caring for the environment in your class. Then every group presents its rules to the "parliament" and the class votes.

Step 1: Write your five rules (5 min)

Step 2: Present and vote (2 min per group)

Present your rules. The other groups ask questions: "Why must we…?" / "Is it a good idea?" Then everybody votes: accept or reject each rule.

    My notes

    Ask Campus Help: an advice column 20 min

    Writing a reply that gives advice

    The university website has a column called "Ask Campus Help". Students send problems and you reply. Choose one message:

    Step 1: Brainstorm advice

    Write five ideas. Choose a modal for each one.

    Step 2: Write your reply

    Write a reply of 60–80 words. Start with "Dear student," and finish with "Good luck!". Use should / shouldn't, must / mustn't, can and might.

    0 words

    Step 3: Check

    Tick each box when it is true.

      Dear student, I understand your problem! You should turn off the notifications on your phone when you study. You can put your phone in another room, and you shouldn't check it every ten minutes. You might also try studying for 25 minutes and then taking a short break. You don't have to study for hours without a rest. Good luck!

      Step 4: Swap and rate

      Exchange replies with a partner. Read the advice. Is it useful?
